subject: Urgent: Latency + 5xx/429 surge on Dedicated - possible transit gateway / NAT / DNS impact
messages:
From: Peter Lowe <plowe@fintechco.com>
To: mina_haddad@redwood.com, rachel_kim@redwood.com
Cc: FintechCo SRE <sre@fintechco.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 08:12:30 -0800
Subject: Latency and 5xx surge - dedicated cluster [FintechCo prod]

Mina / Rachel,

We began seeing a large spike in latency and 5xx/429 errors hitting our production traffic on the dedicated deployment at ~06:40 PST this morning. Error rate climbed from ~0.5% to ~18% over ~6 minutes, with a correlated increase in timeouts at our ingress (client-side). Our SREs captured some packet traces and logs (attached) showing:
- large number of TCP retransmits and reset streams to the Redw-server IPs
- repeated NAT translations failing (SRC ports seem to be reused / missing mappings)
- DNS lookups resolving to different AZ IPs around the spike window

We've already failed over a subset of traffic to our fallback region which helped but we're still seeing elevated 5xxs for API calls routed through your dedicated VPC peer. Can you confirm whether there were any planned changes on the Redwood side (route updates, transit gateway adjustments) or whether you've observed NAT port exhaustion / ephemeral port contention in the dedicated fleet?

We need a bridge now to triage — we're on-call and will keep the packet capture and logs streaming. This is high-impact for FintechCo payment flows.

Attaching: fintech-pcap-20261109.pcap, redwood_gateway_trace.log

Thanks,
Peter
Peter Lowe
Head of Platform — FintechCo
plowe@fintechco.com

From: mina_haddad@redwood.com <mina_haddad@redwood.com>

Cc: rachel_kim@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 08:35:12 -08:00
Subject: Re: Latency and 5xx surge - dedicated cluster [FintechCo prod]

Thanks Peter — scheduling a triage bridge now.

Quick initial notes from our side (SRE team):
- No scheduled maintenance or route changes recorded for the customer's dedicated pool at 06:30–07:00 PST.
- We see a transient spike in connection errors from a subset of nodes behind the customer's VPC peer. Initial metric correlation shows increased SYN retransmits and a sharp rise in 504/522-style timeouts.
- Potential vectors: transit-gateway route convergence (asymmetric path), SNAT port exhaustion on NAT gateway instances, and DNS TTL/propagation anomaly leading to inter-AZ misrouting.

Immediate mitigations we will attempt in parallel:
1) Open bridge (joining details below) — please stay on the call and keep packet capture running.
2) Request FintechCo to hold non-essential retries for 15m (retry amplification is worsening the surge).
3) From Redwood side: temporarily increase SNAT ephemeral port pool on affected NAT instances, and push failover for the customer's route to an alternate egress pool.
4) Short-term DNS cache refresh / reduce resolver TTL to avoid stale mappings while we diagnose.

We will also capture per-node NAT table sizes and ephemeral port utilization and compare with the packet capture. I'll loop in Sean for exec awareness and to authorize credits if this is a platform issue.

Bridge: meet.redwood.com/triage-fintechco (PIN 7782)

—
Mina Haddad
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com

Thanks for the fast triage everyone — good bridge. Quick summary and actions (for the exec thread and post-incident comms):

Timeline (preliminary):
- 06:39:45 PST — transient BGP withdrawal observed on the TGW (22s)
- 06:40:10 PST — client retries amplify; elevated SYN retransmits / 5xx rate spikes to ~18%
- 06:41–06:47 PST — NAT translation table on affected instance reached >94% usage; ephemeral port reuse observed causing reset storms
- 06:48 PST — we kicked failover to alternate egress pool; errors drop to ~1.5% and customer reports improved latency

Root-cause hypothesis (initial):
- Transit gateway route convergence (BGP flap/withdrawal) created a brief asymmetry in return path. That asymmetry, combined with heavy retrying from clients, led to SNAT table pressure on the dedicated NAT instance and ephemeral port exhaustion. The result was a cascade of connection resets and elevated 5xx/429.

Immediate remediation taken:
1) Per customer request we increased ephemeral port pool on the affected NAT instance and moved FintechCo to an alternate egress pool.
2) We set short-term DNS TTL reductions (applying to internal resolvers) and forced cache invalidation to avoid sticky mapping to the flaky egress IPs.
3) Implemented a soft retry throttling recommendation for the customer's SDK (ask them to backoff retries for 2–5 minutes during failover windows).

Next steps / owner list:
- Network SRE (rachel_kim) — deep packet analysis, TGW BGP logs correlation, and SNAT codepath review (owner: rachel_kim). ETA: 48 hours for initial postmortem.
- Platform Reliability (sean_gallagher) — evaluate hardening: increase default ephemeral port pool for dedicated NATs, add early-warning metric for SNAT usage, and automated route failover policy. ETA: 2 weeks for rollout of monitoring + 8 weeks for full mitigation roadmap.
- CS / Accounts (mina_haddad) — draft customer-facing incident letter and credit proposal (owner: mina_haddad). ETA: draft by EOD tomorrow.

Proposed customer communication points: timeline, immediate mitigation steps, interim mitigations (port pool/reroute), root-cause hypothesis, and commitments (monitoring + postmortem).

I'll coordinate the exec briefing and put together a one-page summary for FintechCo leadership. Mina — take point on credits after you gather the exact uptime impact.

Sean Gallagher
VP, Platform Reliability — Redwood Inference
